blocks.source: Salvete Sancti Martyres, Marcelline et Petre: Salvete Christi pugiles, Romulides Athletae.
blocks.english:
Hail, holy Martyrs,
Marcellinus and Peter;
Hail, champions of Christ,
Athletes of Rome.

blocks.source: Illuminastis Ethnicos, Christi fidem serendo: Romae imbuistis barbaros, Verum Deum docendo.
blocks.english:
Ye enlightened the heathen
By sowing the faith of Christ;
In Rome ye instructed the barbarians
By teaching the true God.

blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Propitiare, quaesumus Domine, nobis famulis tuis, per Sanctorum Martyrum tuorum Marcellini et Petri aliorumque Patronorum nostrorum merita gloriosa: ut eorum pia intercessione, ab omnibus protegamar adversis. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Be gracious, we beseech Thee, O Lord, to us Thy servants, through the glorious merits of Thy holy Martyrs Marcellinus and Peter and our other patrons, that by their loving intercession we may be protected from every adversity. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who with Thee liveth and reigneth in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints protegamar, an irregular form. The protection reading in the prepared English remains provisional; the Latin is unchanged.

blocks.source: Familias vos integras Baptismate sacrastis:
blocks.english:
Ye consecrated entire households
By baptism;

blocks.source: Et Daemonum vos copias Signo Crucis fugastis.
blocks.english:
And ye put hosts of demons to flight
By the sign of the Cross.

blocks.source: Vos ne malo consentiam, Ah! impetrate lumen, Amore Dei ut ardeam, Vos invocate Numen.
blocks.english:
Ah, obtain light for me,
That I may not consent to evil;
Invoke the Godhead
That I may burn with love of God.

blocks.source: Praeclara Luminaria, Estis poli solique: Ceu viva exemplaria Placetis vos cuique.
blocks.english:
Ye are glorious lights
Of heaven and earth;
Like living examples
Ye are pleasing to each.

blocks.source: Ah Lumen oro spargite! Ne mens fess’ opprimatur Ne criminum caligine Ne corpus obruatur.
blocks.english:
Ah, I pray, shed light!
Let not the weary mind be oppressed,
Nor by the darkness of crimes
Let the body be overwhelmed.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed shortened “fess’” and the double “Ne” make the syntax compressed; the weary mind/body reading is provisional.

blocks.source: Ut nocte caeli sidera In axibus nitescunt, Ut vere florum germina In hortulis virescunt:
blocks.english:
As the stars of heaven shine
In their courses at night,
As the shoots of flowers grow green
In gardens in spring,

blocks.source: Sic estis ambo fulgidi, Ardore caritatis: Sic estis ambo lucidi, Fulgore castitatis.

So ye both shine
With the ardour of charity;
So ye both are luminous
With the splendour of chastity.

blocks.source: Avete Christi milites, Caeliique Candidati: Fuso cruore nobiles, Ac asperis probati:
blocks.english:
Hail, soldiers of Christ,
Candidates for heaven,
Noble through blood poured forth
And tried by hardships;

blocks.source: Rosas rubore vincitis, Quas Flora purpuravit; Judex rubore sanguinis Serenus vos notavit.
blocks.english:
Ye surpass in redness the roses
Which Flora made purple;
The serene Judge marked you
With the redness of blood.

blocks.source: Vicistis enses, carceres, Minas, rotas, catenas, Stramenta vitri, acinaces Virgasque flagris plenas:
blocks.english:
Ye overcame swords, prisons,
Threats, wheels, chains,
Beds of glass, scimitars,
And rods full of scourges;

blocks.source: Ut dura latus perferam, Cor impetrate forte:
blocks.english:
Obtain for me a strong heart,
That I may endure hard things gladly;
blocks.editorialNote: The PDF prints “latus”; “gladly” is a conjectural reading rather than a Latin correction.

blocks.source: Beatus ut sic gaudeam Cum caelica cohorte.

Be to the Trinity

[The printed “Per infinita vastas” is unresolved.]

blocks.source: Vos purpuratos Pugiles, Nunc ore praedicamus; Et Laureatos Martyres Ex corde honoramus:
blocks.english:
We now proclaim with our mouth
You, champions clothed in purple,
And honour from our hearts
The crowned Martyrs;

blocks.source: In arduis laboribus Ad sanguinem stetistis Fame, siti, sudoribus, Pericula quot subistis?
blocks.english:
In arduous labours
Ye stood firm unto bloodshed;
In hunger, thirst and sweat,
How many perils did ye undergo?

blocks.source: Beata vere Civitas In quam ossa portavit Einhardus: ejus incolas His valde nam beavit.
blocks.english:
Truly blessed is the city
Into which Einhard bore your bones;
For he greatly blessed
Its inhabitants with them.

blocks.source: Stupent Nepotum saecula Miracula, quae patrastis: Et gratiarum flumina Quaeis Patriam rigastis.
blocks.english:
The generations of descendants marvel
At the miracles ye wrought,
And the streams of graces
With which ye watered your homeland.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “Quaeis”; the English “with which” is provisional.

blocks.source: Vidi Civitatem sanctam, habentem claritatem Dei vivi: et Civitas non eget Sole neque Luna; et Reges terrae afferent gloriam suam et honorem in illam.
blocks.english: I saw the holy city, having the brightness of the living God; and the city needs neither sun nor moon, and the kings of the earth shall bring their glory and honour into it.

blocks.source: ℣. Dominus custodiat ossa eorum.
blocks.english: ℣. May the Lord guard their bones.

blocks.source: ℟. Unum ex his non conteretur. (Ps. 33)
blocks.english: ℟. Not one of these shall be broken. (Ps. 33)

blocks.source: ℣. Domine exaudi orationem meam.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

blocks.source: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te veniat.
blocks.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto Thee.

blocks.source: ℣. Benedicamus Domino.
blocks.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Deo gratias.
blocks.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

blocks.source: ℣. Fidelium animae per misericordiam Dei requiescant in pace.
blocks.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful departed, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

blocks.source: ℟. Amen.
blocks.english: ℟. Amen.

blocks.source: Eja beati Caelites Cives Sion beatae! Audite nos superstites, Et semper adjuvate.
blocks.english:
Come, blessed heavenly ones,
Citizens of blessed Sion!
Hear us who remain alive,
And always help us.

blocks.source: Si mortis hora venerit, Juvate morientes: Si cuncta mors absorpserit, Tutate tunc Clientes.
blocks.english:
When the hour of death comes,
Help us as we die;
When death has swallowed all,
Then protect your clients.

blocks.source: Ex orbis hujus orbita, Ah! semitam parate: Ac ad Dei nos atria Tunc, obsecro, vocate. Amen.
blocks.english:
Ah, prepare a path
Out of this world’s course,
And then, I beseech you, call us
Into the courts of God. Amen.

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. All eight hours and the Oblatio remain. The abbreviated Psalm 18 citation remains split across its original rows. No collect is inserted into hours that do not print one. Printed scriptural book and chapter attributions, including their apparent discrepancies, are preserved without correction.
